resolved_by: The Supreme Court in Dean v. United States resolved the split by holding that sentencing courts may consider § 924(c) mandatory minimums when sentencing for the predicate offenses. The Seventh Circuit treats Dean as the resolution.
issue: Did the Supreme Court's Dean decision announce a new rule that applies retroactively on collateral review, so that a federal prisoner whose sentence was set under the prior Eighth Circuit rule can use it?
provision: 18 U.S.C. § 924(c); 28 U.S.C. § 2255 (retroactivity under Teague v. Lane)

sides.position: Before Dean, sentencing courts in the Eighth Circuit were precluded from exercising discretion to account for § 924(c) mandatory minimums when sentencing on the predicate offenses.
cases: United States v. Dean, 810 F.3d 521 (8th Cir. 2015)

quote: Put diﬀerently, it took the Supreme Court deciding Dean to reveal the error in the Eighth Circuit’s law, settle a circuit split, and announce a new rule.
cite: John Worman v. Frederick Entzel, No. 19-2048 (7th Cir. 2020)
